I say “near perfect” in the sense that the car is in exceptional condition for a 20-year-old car but does have its minor imperfections. I’ll list them below. I don’t want to sell this truck, but I don’t need it. Give it a good home.  Call or text Justin (or email, though I might miss it for a day or two): 6wun9.8tu0.7neinnein7

There are still improvements to be made for the next owner, but it is completely drivable and nice in its current state.   We have lots of documentation. We have a miata specific car cover. I have some various extra parts as well.   Let’s get down to it. The car has an 8 psi Jackson Racing M45 supercharger kit installed. The kit runs a MSD NA6 ignition and timing controller as a piggyback to the stock ecu. There is no other tune or ecu required. It is a bit old school but gets the job done as it is specific to this car and kit. Somebody could run a stand alone unit, but my guess is that the gains would be marginal to the cost and headache if changed. It just runs well and sounds amazing, but it is not a rocket ship by any means. My guess is it makes around 150whp in cool weather. Because it is not intercooled, power does drop as the temp increases and can create heat-soak to the supercharger itself. There are intercooler kits if needed. Don’t get me wrong though, a stock NA6 miata probably would be lucky to make 100whp, so this is significantly more powerful.   Other mods included a Flyin Miata suspension kit with the springs and Tokico adjustable shocks. Sway bar kit. Exhaust. Wilwood front brake kit from 949 Racing. Nardi leather steering wheel. Kosei wheels with Conti Extreme tires.   The best part about this car and top selling point is the chassis condition.  No rust (for real) and the body/paint are still very nice. The interior is very clean. The car looks very stock with subtle modifications. It is great.   It could use rear brakes. The timing belt was done within the last 40k but that was years ago. 1951 Chevy Rat Rod Pick-Up  Purchased roughly 10 years ago from a "place down south that specializes in these conversions", the current owner realized that what he purchased still needed some work to be street safe and a viable performance rig.  What he has is a 1951 Chevy 3100 Pick Up truck, situated on a 1990 Chevrolet S-10 chassis. He purchased the truck already converted. The current set-up is running a TBI 4.3L V6 with less than 90K miles on it (according to what he was told when he purchased it) hooked to a 4L60 automatic transmission. It has a single exhaust, routed out through a glass pack muffler. Over the first several years of ownership, he replaced the lower A-arms, all steering components and bushings (tie-rods, steering links), added new springs and shocks, in the rear he replaced the shocks and did new brakes (Disc-F, Drums-R). He added new tires and wheels (Riddler aluminum and Kumho 245/45 ZR18 Ecsta's in front and 275/40 ZR18's out back) and was planning on a V8 swap, when his daughter got into racing 1/4 midget cars, carts and a couple of other classes and since then his time has been totally focused on that. The truck was relegated to a space in the back of the garage and aside from starting to move it around (and rarely take it for a quick blast down the road), it hasn't really been driven in the last couple of years. It's now time to move it on to someone who will enjoy it the way it was designed.  The interior sports a custom Mexican blanket theme with door cards matching the seat material (it IS attached, not just thrown over the old seat). The Dolphin Classic gauges he installed have not yet been hooked up to the S-10 computer. All lights work. The 4.3L V6 has an AC compressor, so if someone wanted to source a condenser and some duct work they could have AC. Truck currently does not have a heater set up. It does have power steering and power brakes.  The truck starts right up and drives very well... with the low center of gravity and the wide, sticky tires she drives almost like a sports car.. almost.  The body is rusty here and there.. but this is a Rat Rod truck, not a shiny, show truck.  Although currently equipped with the V6, a Chevy 350 V8, out of a 71 Nova (reportedly 255HP/280lbft) comes with the truck, along with a stained bed kit, shorty headers, new cab corner, headlight bezel and new windshield.  One can hop into this truck and start enjoying it immediately and then do the V8 swap and add on the other bits while enjoying it or, dive right in and swap in the V8, finish it and then go have fun.  Either way, with all the included parts, asking price is a negotiable $18,000.  Any questions, to schedule a time to see her in person or to make an offer, please don't hesitate to contact me.  Thank you for the interest.

The front spindles are 37 Ford, with 40 Ford backing plates, hydraulic brakes, front and rear, 39 Ford "wide five" drums and rims, with black wall Firestone 6.00-16 tires on front, and Firestone 7.50-16 tires on back."period correct". This completes the front suspension. The 32 frame is boxed, with cross members to support the front spring, the 1961 Chevrolet 283, engine, with exhaust cutouts in the sides of the 32 frame, (VERY COOL), the turbo 350 automatic transmission, and the 1940 Ford rear end with 378 gears, and friction shocks. The rear frame "kickups"are extended to support the body, and the end of the frame has another  2x3"cross member for strength, and to mount the rear spring. This is a vehicle that proudly boasts of solid axles, removable doors, exposed hinges and a fold-down windshield. Yet these symbols of antiquated automotive engineering remain strangely appealing because the Wrangler is still the world's most iconic off-road adventure vehicle.See, those doors have straps because they can be completely removed from the hinges. Ditto the folding windshield, which also comes in handy for hunting the occasional water buffalo. And with 10.2 inches of available ground clearance, solid axles and a steep approach angle, you'll be able to track down that water buffalo on just about whatever terrain it may choose to hide.The big news for the 2011 Wrangler is its revised interior; it's part of Jeep's attempt to become more appealing to mainstream drivers. There's certainly a cognitive dissonance associated with adding new luxury features like heated leather seats, automatic climate control and a steering wheel with audio controls to a cabin that you can clean out with a hose, but then not everyone uses a Wrangler to its most rugged, dirty potential.The 2011 Jeep Wrangler is a unique experience to be sure. This isn't to say it's the only game in town; if you'd like something more civilized that retains much of the Wrangler's off-road talent and visual machismo, the 2011 Nissan Xterra and 2011 Toyota FJ Cruiser are worthy alternatives. Yet for better or for worse, nothing matches the Wrangler's array of unique talents, foibles and quirks. The first serious pro reviews summarize "only adequate body control and moderate roll"...yech!   I doubt that handling can be improved without serious expense by replacing the newbies' OE struts and springs, as there will probably NOT be a "lucky" fix as I discovered for the 2015.5-2019 models via the STi swaybar.  Outside of direct injection (Toyota's forte) the new 2020 design seems derivative rather than seriously revised. Does the +$4k upcharge for the turbo 2.4L motor in the OB XT get you a better suspension and handling? Nope! I pushed a new one through the twisties last spring and was mightily unimpressed. Slow tip-in and turbo lag don't even make it quicker in spontaneous urban driving maneuvers. Sigh.... It's really too bad that I cannot recommend purchasing a new OB. Maybe there'll be a 2022-23 "refresh" to reduce turbo lag and perhaps a stiffer suspension? But that's not Toyoburu's mindset...they're selling cushy SUVs. Even the lower 2020+ Legacy Sedan Limited is unacceptably "loose and cushy" according to automotive press. Didn't need to be....  In conclusion, I've become quite enamored of the best (modified) 2016-2019 Outback 2.5i Premium and Limiteds for those who need a modern 5 door Subie with excellent city and fast highway use, and strongly suggest their purchase over the sloppy 2010-'12 predecessors or CVT failure-prone 2010-2014 (or UNmodified 2015+ Premiums on spongy SUV/truck tires).  The 2019+ new Forester is essentially a sloppy-handling truck/SUV. Forget it. The bloom's off the rose there, despite the frothy initial press and Consumer Reports' current Forest-ophilia...they're so crossover-focused they almost completely ignore the outstanding Outback wagon....  Call or write anytime for a careful focusing consult to help determine which Subie best fits your specific needs, and be careful out there: Subaru-fishing is NOT child's play...especially with older specimens if you're on a budget.  Cheers. Ernie Meunier TheSubaruGuru 781 483-3922 Location: Arlington/WestMedford

I am selling my 1970 Ford Mustang Grande'.  I runs and drives great.  It is in very nice condition.  The Grande' is a rare Mustang trim package, especially after 50 years.  It has been repainted and body panels replaced as needed.  New rear quarters, New roof panel, New floor pans, New vinyl roof.  It looks really nice and gets some attention but it is not "show car" condition so not worth the "big" money that other Mustangs get.  It has the original 302 V8 and 3-speed automatic transmission.  I have not done a lot with the engine.  I have rebuilt the power steering, have replaced the fuel pump and water pump.  I replaced the carburetor with a 4-barrel Holley a few years ago.  I still have original 2150 2-barrel if you want to go back to original.  I have redone most of the interior: new headliner, new dash pad, new interior door panels, new rear seat, new rear deck, new carpet and door sills, new door and window seals.  I replaced the old seats with bucket seats from a 1992 Ford Probe but retained the same seat slides.  If you are a larger adult, you may have a hard time getting into the drivers seat but it is comfortable.  It has a modern radio/CD and new speakers, I added a booster equalizer.  I have not redone the engine or trunk so they look like the 50 year old car that it is.  I have replaced the original mechanical clock in the dash with a digital clock in the same spot. It was originally equipped with A/C but the compressor has not had a belt since I have owned.  I have a clean title for it.  As I said, this is not quite a show quality car.  The bumpers and chrome door handles are pitting and have a little rust.  The paint below the lower body is chipped from rocks, but absolutely zero rust because it never sees rain or snow since being repainted.  If you want to finish the rebuild, all parts can easily be found online.    I am not looking to make a lot of money on it just get out the money I have put into it.  Asking $14000.  Serious inquires only.  If you do not have cash, do not waste your time or mine.  I have a lot of pictures if interested.  Please contact my cell at 3-2-zero-8-zero-8-8611 if interested.  I will not respond to craigslist email replies/questions,  too many scammers.   I do not need help selling the car.   If you just want a nice rare Mustang for summer cruises or easy project to finish this is a great opportunity.

The car has a hybrid automotive grid charger harness hooked up to it, and it will come with the charger itself. (For those who don't know what a plug in grid charger does: a hybrid battery is made up of many cells. During the constant charging and discharging of cells there become a natural imbalance from cell to cell, which cannot be adjusted from the computers. This is also caused by heat, naturally, the cells toward the center of the battery soak up more heat than cells on the outside of the battery, which also causes battery imbalance. As a preventative measure and to increase longevity, the plug in charger is used to recharge the cells as well as rebalance and completely fill every cell. Depending on the driving you do will depend on how frequent it makes sense to plug the charger in. I typically grid charge the car for 24 hours (max) every couple months. The Good We have had this car for about 5 years and it was purchased from a local dealer in Charlotte. The car is a daily driver in good condition. There are a lot of new stuff on the car.  New tires, new struts, new front drive axles. The car has a fresh oil change. The ride is nice and smooth.  My son drove this car regularly to work until recently when he bought a new car.  Just completed NC inspection.  The Not So Good The check engine light is on. It's been on for all the years we have owned the car. It is a cam position sensor light. the sensor has been replaced along with other repairs to try and make the light stay off.  The engine runs fine, passes all the emissions tests. Multiple shops have worked to make the light go way over the years, but since there is no impact on the operation of the car, we have just learned to live with it. The car now is old enough to pass NC inspection with the light on and has a new completed NC inspection. There is a tear in the driver seat and there is wear on both front seats (rear seats are fine). The sunroof headliner fabric is a bit wrinkled. The driver door handle is loose.  This is a fairly common problem on these Volvos. As long as you are careful with it, it works ok.
